case_title.quote: RAMESH AND OTHERS v. STATE OF HARYANA

number_of_accused.quote: thereby convicting all the four accused persons (appellants herein)

accused_gender.quote: Saroj (wife of Suresh) and Prem (her mother in-law)
accused_gender.reason: Accused include two women, Saroj and Prem, besides two men.

accused_age.reason: No age of any accused is given.

accused_occupation.correct_value: Appellant Ramesh had a truck (truck driver/owner implied)
accused_occupation.quote: I was at my in laws house at Nizampur, Delhi along with my truck
accused_occupation.reason: Ramesh's statement mentions his truck, hinting at occupation; the judgment does not state it expressly. Weak but 'Not stated' is arguable.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal record mentioned; only earlier s.107/151 proceedings.

victim_gender.quote: Smt. Roshni, wife of Appellant no. 1

victim_age.correct_value: Not stated (married 20 years; sons aged 16 and 15)
victim_age.quote: My marriage was solemnized 20 years before.
victim_age.reason: Her age is not stated; 25 is inconsistent with a 20-year marriage and a 16-year-old son.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: my husband Ramesh... my devar Suresh... Saroj and Prem
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Only spouse is listed; the other accused are in-laws.

offence_category.quote: offences under Sections 302, 34, 498A of Indian Penal Code
offence_category.reason: Charges were murder and cruelty; s.304-B was not invoked, though the headnote says dowry death.

weapon.quote: Ramesh sprinkled kerosene on her. Suresh lighted a matchstick

evidence_type.correct_value: dying declaration, medical evidence, recovery of kerosene container, witness testimony
evidence_type.reason: Broadly right but omits hostile witness testimony.

confession.reason: No confession; only a disclosure statement leading to recovery.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Victim set ablaze while sleeping; earlier attempt of throwing her in a well; continuous dowry harassment
aggravating_circumstances.quote: One year before the incident, she was even thrown in a well
aggravating_circumstances.reason: The judgment records aggravating facts, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

trial_court_outcome.quote: tried and acquitted by the Sessions Court

high_court_outcome.quote: overturned the verdict of acquittal, thereby convicting all the four accused

final_outcome.quote: We, thus, do not find any merit in this appeal, which is accordingly dismissed.
final_outcome.reason: Substance right but the formal outcome is dismissal of the appeal.

offence_finally_established.quote: Section 498-A/34 IPC:- To undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Rigorous imprisonment for life (s.302) and 2 years RI (s.498-A)
imprisonment_type.quote: To undergo rigorous imprisonment for life

neutral_facts.correct_value: Victim set ablaze at home allegedly by husband, brother-in-law with in-laws holding her; she gave a dying declaration; PW-4 claimed Ramesh was with him.
neutral_facts.quote: Suresh lighted a matchstick and set her ablaze.
neutral_facts.reason: Says husband and brother set her on fire (allegation stated as fact) and reveals PW-4's testimony was found false, an outcome reveal.

offence_severity.quote: rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/-

number_of_offences.correct_value: Two offences (ss.302 and 498-A, with s.34) against four accused
number_of_offences.quote: charges against all the accused persons under Section 302, 498A, IPC with the aid of section 34
number_of_offences.reason: Value is garbled and omits the count of offences.

motive.quote: On some occasion they say to bring buffalo and on some occasion they demand money and scooter.
motive.reason: Motive is dowry demand, not 'dowry death'.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the Doctor made an endorsement... that the deceased remained fit

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-4 found false and won over; PW-3 and PW-4 turned hostile; PW-11 Magistrate believed
witness_credibility.quote: PW-4, though brother of the deceased, appears to have been won over by the appellants.
witness_credibility.reason: Omits PW-3 and the Magistrate's credibility.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused took the victim to hospital; PW-4 shielded Ramesh
post_offence_conduct.quote: it is Ramesh who had brought the deceased to the hospital and got her admitted

legal_representation.quote: Praveen Kr. Aggai-Wal, Upendra Pratap Singh, Sanjay Jain, Advs. for the Appellants

investigation_status.quote: a report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. was presented

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Trial court's approach to dying declaration held legally unsustainable; ignored doctor's certification
procedural_irregularity.quote: the manner in which the trial court proceeded with the matter was legally unsustainable
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment notes the trial court's flawed appreciation, though not a procedural irregularity strictly.

appeal_history.quote: the High Court, in appeal, has overturned the verdict of acquittal

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued the statement was recorded after authorities were satisfied of her fitness, so no reason to discard it
prosecution_argument.quote: The authorities were fully satisfied that she was in a position to give the statement.
prosecution_argument.reason: Roughly right but embellished (e.g., 'presence of medical officer').

defence_argument.correct_value: Two views possible so acquittal should stand; Ramesh was with PW-4 so falsely roped in; 100% burns made statement impossible
defence_argument.quote: even when two views were possible, the High Court should not have tinkered with the acquittal
defence_argument.reason: Omits the acquittal-appeal point; 'unconscious' and 'incoherent' not argued exactly.

legal_principle_applied.quote: this dying declaration cannot be discarded merely going by the extent of burns

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sanwat Singh v. State of Rajasthan 1961 SCR (3) 120
precedent_relied_upon.reason: List matches; 'Krishna Mohi' is a minor typo for Mochi.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The Supreme Court gave no sentencing rationale; deterrence not discussed.
